In insertion, imperfect angular alignment and premature gripper release can make a vial topple from the rack; some failures may become unrecoverable, such as when a vial cannot be reset. context: MaCoPlanner implements proactive safety checking before any physical actuation. Equipment manuals are first compiled into a typed intermediate representation containing procedures, task-level safety constraints, state conditions, parameter specifications, and control relations, with source links retained for evidence retrieval. The planner uses this structured knowledge to generate symbolic action sequences. Each candidate plan is then symbolically rolled out and checked against procedural requirements and device state-transition constraints. When a violation is detected, the system localizes it and sends targeted feedback to the planner for repair. A verified symbolic sequence is passed to a separate execution interface, which grounds actions to physical controls and updates device state. If refinement cannot produce a compliant plan within the allowed repair budget, the plan is rejected rather than executed. Under an independent evaluation oracle, the reported final violation rate is 2.7%. In the repair analysis, 26.3% of runs are rejected after exhausting the refinement budget. Task success improves from 62.8% to 84.4% for Level-2 tasks and from 25.9% to 43.2% for Level-3 tasks compared with Raw-Manual. The experiments use a controller-panel simulator and do not claim industrial deployment readiness.

MaCoPlanner uses typed evidence retrieval and evidence gating to expose task-critical constraints, then verifies generated plans using both Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) and a Safety Finite-State Machine (FSM). Verification evaluates whether a plan reaches the target state under executable action semantics and checks procedural as well as state-dependent safety clauses. Interpreting compliance as the complement of the violation rate, this corresponds to approximately 97.3% safety-clause compliance.
